summary: The Knesset passed an amendment expanding the incoming national security minister's authority over police policy; legal advisers had warned that parts of the proposal threatened police independence, and some clauses were split off before passage. A later High Court ruling in 2025 invalidated the provision allowing ministerial influence over police investigations while leaving other provisions standing.
